overview: Success needs in-depth knowledge of modules 3 and 4 plus practical skills from modules 1 and 2.
Many marks were lost through imprecise definitions, unclear reasoning and missing working.
State the equation, substitute the data, then evaluate; show working so later parts can gain error-carried-forward credit.
In 'show' questions the unknown must be the subject; working backwards from the given value earns nothing.
Practical skills questions exposed weak knowledge of instrument resolution, uncertainty rules and significant figures.
Give quantitative answers (e.g. 'doubles') whenever the question supplies quantitative data.
assessment_for_learning: Know the meanings of thinking, braking and stopping distance.
Gain experience describing experimental methods as well as analysing data.
Use a wide range of lab measuring instruments and know their resolutions.
When quantities are added or subtracted, add their absolute uncertainties (see the Practical Skills Handbook).
Understand significant figures including trailing zeros (0.06 is 1 s.f.; 0.060 is 2 s.f.).
Use consistent units and know common prefixes.
Be able to convert between fractions of a wavelength, degrees and radians.
See practically how ammeter and voltmeter readings change with external resistance when a cell has internal resistance, and practise explaining it.
Understand the differences between the photoelectric effect and electron diffraction.
Practise describing the effect of doubling/halving one quantity on another.
